Camila,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday — OrbitMed's procurement/legal team took a pass on the draft order form and attached a redline focused on the pricing exhibit. High level asks:

- Carve out for high-throughput bursts (we've highlighted a narrow exception window for months 1-3).
- Clarify the relationship between caps and floor true-ups (we added language that ties any cap adjustment to the three-month trailing usage baseline).
- Add an SLO credit mechanism: OrbitMed wants a clear, formulaic credit tied to 99.9% token-level SLO, capped at 5% of monthly fees and amortized across the following month.

We're attaching our annotated doc (orbitmed_redline_10-03.docx) — redlines in track changes. Procurement would like to close the commercial terms this week so legal can finalize the DocuSign packet.

Anna — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Appreciated. High-level response before Karthik/Marissa weigh in:

- Burst carveout: we are open to a limited initial burst window but need to limit the duration and explicit volume threshold (otherwise it undermines pricing guarantees). Suggested: first 60–90 days, capped at X tokens per day per customer. Can you confirm expected burst sizing so we can quantify impact?
- Cap/floor true-ups: we prefer an operating model that recalibrates caps based on rolling usage but won't accept an open-ended retrospective pricing change that materially affects already-invoiced months. We can accept a three-month trailing baseline if the change is prospective and accompanied by a notice window.
- SLO credits: Redwood's preference is amortized credits (spread across the next invoice cycle) for predictable cashflow. We can accept a 5% cap on monthly fees but want a two-tier remediation (credit for transient SLO misses; escalation path to termination only after repeated breaches).

Looping in Karthik on the finance/ops sizing and Marissa on legal wording. We can take a markup pass on your doc and return a counter by tomorrow EOD.

—Camila

Anna / Camila — quick note from finance/ops:

We ran a sensitivity on a 90-day burst carveout vs. a 60-day carveout with a daily token cap. Findings:
- 60-day carveout with a 10M token/day hard cap increases expected unit cost by ~3.7% vs. base case.
- 90-day increases ~5.6%.

Proposal (compromise):
- Accept a 60-day burst carveout, daily cap at X tokens (we'll use the language 'burst allowance not to exceed 10M tokens/day unless mutually agreed in writing').
- Cap/floor true-ups: accept a three-month trailing baseline for prospective cap adjustments with a 30-day notice and no retroactive invoice changes.
- SLO credit: accept amortized credit limited to 5% monthly fees. Credit calculation we propose: (monthly_fee * min(0.05, (SLO_shortfall_hours / total_production_hours))) — credit applied pro-rata across the next invoice. We can provide the explicit formula in the order form exhibit.

Attached is our suggested exhibit markup (orderform_v3-pricing-exhibit-markup.pdf) showing language and the sample formula. If those knobs look workable we'll have legal prepare a tightened clause.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: orderform_v3-pricing-exhibit-markup.pdf]

Date: 2027-10-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline: pricing exhibit caps/floors + proposed SLO credit

Thanks Karthik — the sensitivity framing helps. OrbitMed can accept the 60-day burst window at the 10M token/day cap. A few clarifications before we finalize wording:

1) Definition of "SLO shortfall hours" — we want the metric to be tied to token-rate availability (not per-model) and to be computed using Redwood's monitoring traces with a mutually agreed time-series aggregation. Please propose the exact metric name (e.g., token_availability_5m_pct) we can reference in the exhibit.
2) Notice periods — procurement needs a 45-day notice for any prospective cap increase (we can be flexible on decreases).
3) Whitelisting fallback — in cases of region-level outage, can we add a clause that allows temporary fallback to a compatible model variant without reprice for up to 7 days? This helps our SREs maintain continuity.

We updated the redline with those asks and uploaded the file to the Drive link above. If we get your final language today, procurement will get DocuSign out tomorrow morning.

Anna
Anna Li
Senior Counsel, OrbitMed

Anna — adding legal's final language edits inline below. Overall position: we can accept the commercial compromise as outlined (60-day burst at 10M token/day, prospective cap adjustments with 30-day notice, amortized SLO credit capped at 5%). Key legal clarifications we added:

- Bursts: tightened the definition and added an explicit exclusion for abusive automated traffic; Redwood retains right to throttle if token abuse observed.
- Prospective adjustments: clarified that any cap increases require mutual written agreement if the increase exceeds 15% of the trailing baseline — this protects OrbitMed from surprise material increases.
- SLO credit formula: included the exact formula Karthik proposed, added an audit right for OrbitMed to request aggregated traces for credit calculations (limited to 2 requests per year), and added a dispute escalation path (service credits, remediation plan, then C-suite review if unresolved).

I have attached the redline with track changes and a short summary for procurement to include in the DocuSign package. Camila — please confirm you want me to accept these edits and prepare a final 'Order Form — Exhibit B (Pricing)' to send for signature.
